statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 1
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter I: Preliminary
title: Short Title, Extent and Commencement
penalty: Up to Rs. 50 Crore under Schedule Item 7
official_text: This Act may be called the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may appoint.
technical_implication: Applies across all digital applications processing personal data of Indian citizens.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 2
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter I: Preliminary
title: Key Statutory Definitions (Data Fiduciary, Principal, Breach, Processing)
penalty: Up to Rs. 50 Crore under Schedule Item 7
official_text: Defines Data Fiduciary as any person who alone or in conjunction with other persons determines the purpose and means of processing; Data Principal as the individual to whom personal data relates; Personal Data Breach as any unauthorised processing, disclosure, destruction or compromise.
technical_implication: Defines roles and scopes for system architecture and entity responsibility models.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 3
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter I: Preliminary
title: Application of the Act to Digital Personal Data & Extraterritorial Reach
penalty: Up to Rs. 50 Crore under Schedule Item 7
official_text: Applies to the processing of digital personal data within the territory of India where collected in digital form or digitized subsequently, and applies outside India if offering goods or services to Data Principals in India.
technical_implication: Enforces compliance on both domestic infrastructure and offshore cloud services catering to Indian users.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 4
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter II: Obligations of Data Fiduciary
title: Grounds for Lawful Processing of Personal Data
penalty: Up to Rs. 50 Crore under Schedule Item 7
official_text: A person may process the personal data of a Data Principal only in accordance with the provisions of this Act and for a lawful purpose for which the Data Principal has given consent or for certain legitimate uses.
technical_implication: Every data ingestion pipeline, API endpoint, and database store must possess an explicit lawful processing flag (consent or legitimate use) prior to processing.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 5(1) read with Rule 3
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter II: Obligations of Data Fiduciary
title: Itemised Notice Accompanying Consent Request
penalty: Up to Rs. 50 Crore under Schedule Item 7
official_text: Every request made to a Data Principal under section 6 for consent shall be accompanied or preceded by a notice given by the Data Fiduciary informing the personal data and the purpose for which it is processed, manner of exercising rights, and grievance redressal contact.
technical_implication: Requires structured privacy modals disclosing each collected field (itemized list), the exact purpose of collection, and how to reach the Grievance Officer.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 5(3)
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter II: Obligations of Data Fiduciary
title: Multilingual Notice Option (Eighth Schedule Languages)
penalty: Up to Rs. 50 Crore under Schedule Item 7
official_text: The Data Fiduciary shall give the Data Principal the option to access the notice and consent request in English or any language specified in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution of India.
technical_implication: Frontend UI must provide language selection supporting English and Indian Eighth Schedule regional languages (e.g. Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, Bengali, Kannada).

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 6(1) read with Rule 3
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter II: Obligations of Data Fiduciary
title: Lawful Consent: Free, Specific, Informed, Unconditional, Unambiguous & Affirmative
penalty: Up to Rs. 50 Crore under Schedule Item 7
official_text: The consent given by the Data Principal shall be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous with a clear affirmative action, and shall signify an agreement to the processing of personal data for the specified purpose.
technical_implication: Strictly forbids pre-ticked consent checkboxes, forced bundle consent in terms of service, and dark pattern opt-ins; requires explicit affirmative API recording.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 6(4) read with Rule 4
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter II: Obligations of Data Fiduciary
title: Right to Withdraw Consent with Comparable Ease
penalty: Up to Rs. 50 Crore under Schedule Item 7
official_text: The Data Principal shall have the right to withdraw her consent at any time, with the ease of doing so being comparable to the ease with which consent was given.
technical_implication: User settings dashboard must provide 1-click consent revocation with equal simplicity to onboarding, without hiding behind email requests or phone calls.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 6(6)
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter II: Obligations of Data Fiduciary
title: Mandatory Cessation of Processing upon Consent Withdrawal
penalty: Up to Rs. 50 Crore under Schedule Item 7
official_text: Where consent is withdrawn, the Data Fiduciary shall, within a reasonable time, cease and cause its Data Processors to cease processing the personal data of such Data Principal.
technical_implication: Requires real-time pub/sub or webhook event propagation across microservices and processors to halt data flows immediately upon user withdrawal.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 7
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter II: Obligations of Data Fiduciary
title: Processing for Certain Legitimate Uses
penalty: Up to Rs. 50 Crore under Schedule Item 7
official_text: A Data Fiduciary may process personal data of a Data Principal for certain legitimate uses: voluntary provision without opt-out, State subsidies, legal compliance, medical emergency, employment, or epidemic safety.
technical_implication: System must document and audit-trail non-consent based processing under defined statutory exemptions.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 8(2)
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter II: Obligations of Data Fiduciary
title: Engagement of Data Processor under Valid Contract
penalty: Up to Rs. 50 Crore under Schedule Item 7
official_text: A Data Fiduciary may engage, appoint, use or otherwise involve a Data Processor to process personal data on its behalf only under a valid contract.
technical_implication: Third-party APIs, SaaS vendors, and processors must have audited Data Protection Addendums (DPAs) before production API credential issuance.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 8(3)
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter II: Obligations of Data Fiduciary
title: Completeness, Accuracy and Consistency of Personal Data
penalty: Up to Rs. 50 Crore under Schedule Item 7
official_text: A Data Fiduciary shall ensure personal data processed is accurate, complete and consistent if it is used to make a decision that affects the Data Principal or is disclosed to another Data Fiduciary.
technical_implication: Database schemas must implement schema validation, referential integrity, and profile update synchronization across all operational databases.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 8(4)
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter II: Obligations of Data Fiduciary
title: Appropriate Technical and Organisational Measures
penalty: Up to Rs. 50 Crore under Schedule Item 7
official_text: A Data Fiduciary shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure effective observance of the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder.
technical_implication: Requires automated CI/CD security gates, static analysis (.coderabbit.yaml), automated secrets scanning, and vulnerability gating.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 8(5) read with Schedule Item 1
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter II: Obligations of Data Fiduciary
title: Obligation to take Reasonable Security Safeguards to Prevent Personal Data Breach
penalty: Up to Rs. 250 Crore (Two Hundred and Fifty Crore Rupees) under Schedule Item 1
official_text: A Data Fiduciary shall protect personal data in its possession or under its control, including in respect of any processing undertaken by it or on its behalf by a Data Processor, by taking reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breach.
technical_implication: Mandates parameterized queries, strict input validation, memory safety, dynamic code execution prohibition (no eval), end-to-end encryption, and role-based access control to prevent unauthorized exposure.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 8(6) read with Schedule Item 2
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter II: Obligations of Data Fiduciary
title: Mandatory Notification of Personal Data Breach to Board and Affected Data Principals
penalty: Up to Rs. 200 Crore (Two Hundred Crore Rupees) under Schedule Item 2
official_text: In the event of a personal data breach, the Data Fiduciary shall give the Board and each affected Data Principal, intimation of such breach in such form and manner as may be prescribed.
technical_implication: Requires real-time security telemetry, automated alerting hooks, and incident response pipelines capable of dispatching breach intimations to the Board and victims without delay.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 8(7) read with Section 8(8)
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter II: Obligations of Data Fiduciary
title: Erasure of Personal Data upon Purpose Fulfillment or Consent Withdrawal (Storage Limitation)
penalty: Up to Rs. 50 Crore under Schedule Item 7
official_text: A Data Fiduciary shall, unless retention is necessary for compliance with any law, erase personal data upon the Data Principal withdrawing consent or as soon as it is reasonable to assume that the specified purpose is no longer being served.
technical_implication: Requires automated database retention policies, soft-delete expiration workers, cascading deletion across database replicas, and TTL purge workers.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 8(9) read with Section 13
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter II: Obligations of Data Fiduciary
title: Establishment of Effective Grievance Redressal Mechanism
penalty: Up to Rs. 50 Crore under Schedule Item 7
official_text: A Data Fiduciary shall establish an effective mechanism to redress the grievances of Data Principals in respect of any act or omission regarding obligations under this Act.
technical_implication: Application must expose an authenticated support portal or ticketing endpoint allowing Data Principals to log and track privacy grievances.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 8(10) read with Rule 9
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter II: Obligations of Data Fiduciary
title: Publication of Business Contact Details of Data Protection Officer or Grievance Officer
penalty: Up to Rs. 50 Crore under Schedule Item 7
official_text: A Data Fiduciary shall publish the business contact information of a Data Protection Officer, if applicable, or a person who is able to answer on behalf of the Data Fiduciary, the questions of the Data Principal about personal data processing.
technical_implication: Privacy policy, landing pages, and API meta endpoints must publicly list the name, corporate email address, and postal address of the designated Grievance Officer.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 9(1) read with Schedule Item 3
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter II: Obligations of Data Fiduciary
title: Verifiable Consent of Parent or Lawful Guardian for Children
penalty: Up to Rs. 200 Crore (Two Hundred Crore Rupees) under Schedule Item 3
official_text: The Data Fiduciary shall, before processing any personal data of a child or a person with disability who has a lawful guardian, obtain verifiable consent of the parent of such child or lawful guardian in such manner as may be prescribed.
technical_implication: User onboarding must enforce age-gating. For users under 18, verifiable parental OTP, Aadhaar eSign, or DigiLocker guardian verification is legally mandatory.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 9(2) read with Schedule Item 3
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter II: Obligations of Data Fiduciary
title: Prohibition of Processing Causing Detrimental Effect on Child
penalty: Up to Rs. 200 Crore (Two Hundred Crore Rupees) under Schedule Item 3
official_text: A Data Fiduciary shall not undertake such processing of personal data that is likely to cause any detrimental effect on the well-being of a child.
technical_implication: Content algorithms and interaction pipelines must implement strict safety filters preventing harmful content exposure to verified child accounts.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 9(3) read with Schedule Item 3
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter II: Obligations of Data Fiduciary
title: Prohibition of Tracking, Behavioural Monitoring, and Targeted Advertising on Children
penalty: Up to Rs. 200 Crore (Two Hundred Crore Rupees) under Schedule Item 3
official_text: A Data Fiduciary shall not undertake tracking or behavioural monitoring of children or targeted advertising directed at children.
technical_implication: Codebase must unconditionally suppress Google Analytics, Meta Pixel, tracking pixels, device fingerprinting, and ad-tech SDKs for any user under 18 years old.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 10 read with Schedule Item 4
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter II: Obligations of Data Fiduciary
title: Additional Obligations of Significant Data Fiduciary (DPO, Independent Auditor, DPIA)
penalty: Up to Rs. 150 Crore (One Hundred and Fifty Crore Rupees) under Schedule Item 4
official_text: The Central Government may notify any Data Fiduciary as a Significant Data Fiduciary based on factors like volume of data, risk of harm, and sovereignty. A Significant Data Fiduciary shall appoint a resident Data Protection Officer, appoint an independent data auditor, and undertake periodic Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIA).
technical_implication: High-volume platforms must implement formal DPIA templates, cryptographic audit trails for external reviewers, and an executive DPO reporting channel.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 11 read with Rule 11
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter III: Rights and Duties of Data Principal
title: Right of Data Principal to Obtain Information About Personal Data
penalty: Up to Rs. 50 Crore under Schedule Item 7
official_text: The Data Principal shall have the right to obtain from the Data Fiduciary a summary of personal data being processed, identities of all other Data Fiduciaries and Data Processors with whom data has been shared, and any other prescribed information.
technical_implication: Implement authenticated self-service API (e.g. GET /api/user/data-export) producing machine-readable JSON/CSV export of stored personal data and vendor sharing logs.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 12(1) & 12(2)
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter III: Rights and Duties of Data Principal
title: Right to Correction, Completion and Updating of Personal Data
penalty: Up to Rs. 50 Crore under Schedule Item 7
official_text: A Data Principal shall have the right to correction, completion and updating of her personal data for the processing of which she has previously given consent.
technical_implication: Provide profile edit forms and PATCH endpoints allowing users to rectify outdated names, phone numbers, addresses, or emails.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 12(3) read with Section 8(7)
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter III: Rights and Duties of Data Principal
title: Right to Erasure of Personal Data
penalty: Up to Rs. 50 Crore under Schedule Item 7
official_text: A Data Principal shall have the right to erasure of her personal data, and upon receipt of such request the Data Fiduciary shall erase the personal data unless retention is necessary for a legal obligation.
technical_implication: Provide explicit DELETE /api/user/account route triggering cascading deletion across primary database, caches, logs, and downstream processors.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 13 read with Rule 9
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter III: Rights and Duties of Data Principal
title: Right of Grievance Redressal and Timely SLA
penalty: Up to Rs. 50 Crore under Schedule Item 7
official_text: A Data Principal shall have the right to have readily available means of grievance redressal provided by a Data Fiduciary or Consent Manager in respect of any act or omission regarding personal data obligations.
technical_implication: Grievance ticketing must guarantee automated acknowledgment within 24 hours and resolution within statutory SLA (7 to 30 days).

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 14
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter III: Rights and Duties of Data Principal
title: Right to Nominate Representative in Event of Death or Incapacity
penalty: Up to Rs. 50 Crore under Schedule Item 7
official_text: A Data Principal shall have the right to nominate any other individual, who shall, in the event of death or incapacity of the Data Principal, exercise the rights of the Data Principal.
technical_implication: Account settings may implement an optional digital nominee feature allowing account transfer or closure upon certified incapacity.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 15 read with Schedule Item 5
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter III: Rights and Duties of Data Principal
title: Duties of Data Principal (Prohibition of Impersonation and Frivolous Claims)
penalty: Up to Rs. 10,000 under Schedule Item 5
official_text: A Data Principal shall not impersonate another person, suppress material information, register false or frivolous grievances, or furnish false particulars.
technical_implication: Implement rate limiting and CAPTCHA/identity verification on grievance submission forms to mitigate automated grievance abuse.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 16 read with Rule 5
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter IV: Special Provisions
title: Cross-Border Transfer Restrictions of Personal Data Outside India
penalty: Up to Rs. 50 Crore under Schedule Item 7
official_text: The Central Government may, by notification, restrict the transfer of personal data by a Data Fiduciary for processing to such country or territory outside India as may be so notified.
technical_implication: Outbound HTTP requests, external SDKs, foreign cloud endpoints, and SSRF destinations must be verified against government transfer negative-lists.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 17
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter IV: Special Provisions
title: Statutory Exemptions (Legal Enforcement, Research, Archiving, Startups)
penalty: Up to Rs. 50 Crore under Schedule Item 7
official_text: Exempts processing necessary for enforcing legal rights, court orders, investigation of offences, research, archiving or statistical purposes, or notified fintech/startup entities.
technical_implication: System should record statutory exemption tags when logging personal data for legal subpoena or compliance preservation.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 28 & 29
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter VII: Appeal and Alternate Dispute Resolution
title: Appeals to Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT)
penalty: Up to Rs. 50 Crore under Schedule Item 7
official_text: Any person aggrieved by an order or direction made by the Data Protection Board may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT) within thirty days.
technical_implication: Legal and compliance systems must retain immutable evidence bundles for 60 days following any Board inquiry.

statutory_citation: DPDP Act 2023, Section 33 read with The Schedule
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
chapter: Chapter VIII: Penalties and Adjudication
title: Comprehensive Schedule of Statutory Monetary Penalties (Items 1 to 7)
penalty: Up to Rs. 250 Crore per violation
official_text: Prescribes statutory fines: Item 1: Failure to take reasonable security safeguards under 8(5) - up to Rs. 250 Crore; Item 2: Failure to notify breach under 8(6) - up to Rs. 200 Crore; Item 3: Failure regarding children under Sec 9 - up to Rs. 200 Crore; Item 4: Significant Data Fiduciary failure under Sec 10 - up to Rs. 150 Crore; Item 5: Data Principal duty breach under Sec 15 - up to Rs. 10,000; Item 7: General non-compliance - up to Rs. 50 Crore.
technical_implication: Assesses monetary risk exposure across all code defects and architecture non-compliances.

statutory_citation: DPDP Rules 2025, Rules 3 & 4 (SARAL Standalone Consent Architecture)
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (Notified by MeitY)
chapter: Part I: Notice & Consent Specifications
title: SARAL Framework for Standalone Consent Notices and Consent Manager Integration
penalty: Up to Rs. 50 Crore under DPDP Act Schedule Item 7
official_text: Consent notices must be independent of general terms and conditions, presented in clear plain language adhering to the SARAL standard, specifying purpose-to-data mapping, and providing direct integration with registered Consent Managers.
technical_implication: Requires dedicated consent modals with granular purpose toggles and registered consent manager API webhooks.

statutory_citation: DPDP Rules 2025, Rule 5 (Cross-Border Transfer Safeguards)
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (Notified by MeitY)
chapter: Part II: Cross-Border Data Flow
title: Cross-Border Transfer Due Diligence, Standard Clauses & Auditing
penalty: Up to Rs. 50 Crore under DPDP Act Schedule Item 7
official_text: Data Fiduciaries transmitting personal data overseas must execute standard contractual clauses ensuring equivalent safeguards, enforce end-to-end encryption, and verify recipient jurisdictions against MeitY notification lists.
technical_implication: Outbound egress proxies must enforce destination IP filtering and TLS 1.3 for all external transfers.

statutory_citation: DPDP Rules 2025, Rule 6 (Mandatory Security Safeguards & Encryption Standards)
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (Notified by MeitY)
chapter: Part II: Security and Technical Safeguards
title: Mandatory Technical Security Safeguards, Encryption, and Access Controls
penalty: Up to Rs. 250 Crore under DPDP Act Schedule Item 1 read with Section 8(5)
official_text: Data Fiduciaries shall implement technical safeguards including encryption at rest using AES-256 or equivalent standards, encryption in transit via TLS 1.3, strict role-based access control, secure key management, and cryptographic protection of credentials and sensitive identifiers.
technical_implication: Bans MD5, SHA-1, ECB mode, plaintext passwords, unencrypted Aadhaar/PAN storage, and requires httpOnly/secure cookies.

statutory_citation: DPDP Rules 2025, Rule 7 (Breach Reporting Protocols & 6-Hour Timelines)
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (Notified by MeitY)
chapter: Part II: Breach Notification and Incident Response
title: Prescribed Form, Manner, and 6-Hour Timeline for Breach Notification
penalty: Up to Rs. 200 Crore under DPDP Act Schedule Item 2 read with Section 8(6)
official_text: Upon becoming aware of a personal data breach, the Data Fiduciary shall intimate the Board within 6 hours with preliminary incident details, followed by a comprehensive forensic report, and inform affected Data Principals without undue delay.
technical_implication: Automated incident dispatch workflows must trigger within 6 hours of high-severity exfiltration or compromise.

statutory_citation: DPDP Rules 2025, Rule 8 (Age Verification Standards for Minors)
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (Notified by MeitY)
chapter: Part III: Children's Privacy Standards
title: Approved Age Verification and Parental Verification Mechanisms
penalty: Up to Rs. 200 Crore under DPDP Act Schedule Item 3 read with Section 9
official_text: Data Fiduciaries must deploy approved methods to verify that an onboarding user is an adult or obtain verifiable guardian consent through electronic verification tokens, government ID gateways, or DigiLocker integration.
technical_implication: Integrate certified Indian identity tokens or guardian verification APIs prior to permitting minor onboarding.

statutory_citation: DPDP Rules 2025, Rule 9 (Grievance Redressal Timelines & DPO Specifications)
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (Notified by MeitY)
chapter: Part IV: Grievance Redressal Process
title: Grievance Officer SLA: 24-Hour Acknowledgment and 15-Day Resolution
penalty: Up to Rs. 50 Crore under DPDP Act Schedule Item 7
official_text: The Grievance Redressal Officer shall acknowledge any complaint from a Data Principal within twenty-four hours and resolve the grievance within fifteen calendar days.
technical_implication: Automated helpdesk pipelines must auto-ack tickets within 24 hours and enforce an SLA timer alerting managers if unresolved by day 10.

statutory_citation: DPDP Rules 2025, Rule 10 (Data Protection Impact Assessment Methodology)
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (Notified by MeitY)
chapter: Part V: Significant Data Fiduciary Governance
title: Standards and Methodology for Periodic DPIA and Independent Data Audits
penalty: Up to Rs. 150 Crore under DPDP Act Schedule Item 4 read with Section 10
official_text: Significant Data Fiduciaries must conduct annual independent data audits by certified auditors and perform Data Protection Impact Assessments prior to deploying new automated processing, AI models, or biometric profiling.
technical_implication: Requires documented risk matrices and audit log exports for machine learning model training and inference pipelines.

statutory_citation: DPDP Rules 2025, Rule 11 (Data Portability and Access Rights Procedures)
law: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (Notified by MeitY)
chapter: Part VI: Data Principal Rights Fulfillment
title: Electronic Formats and Verification for Data Subject Access Requests (DSAR)
penalty: Up to Rs. 50 Crore under DPDP Act Schedule Item 7
official_text: Upon request by a Data Principal under section 11, the Data Fiduciary shall provide the summary of personal data in structured, commonly used and machine-readable electronic format within 7 days.
technical_implication: Endpoint generating user export must provide password-protected, encrypted zip or standardized JSON payload within 7 business days.
